extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers / experimental scientists (readers of Philosophical Transactions)
extracted.subtask_description: Rubric-like standards and practical criteria embedded in an early-18th-century Philosophical Transactions issue for conducting and judging observations, experiments, and historical/analytic arguments in natural philosophy (observational reports, experimental descriptions, and inferential reasoning).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use direct empirical observation to support theories (example: springs/dew)
rubrics_metrics.description: Now this theory of springs is not a bare hypothesis, but founded on experience, which it was my luck to gain in my stay at St. Helena, where in the night time, on the tops of the hills ... the dew would fall so fast ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support physical theories with concrete, repeated natural observations (e.g., frequency and effects of dew/condensation on instruments and papers). Report specific circumstances (location, altitude, how observations interfered with work) so observations constitute evidence rather than conjecture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Microscopic observation of rudiments in eggs as evidential standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Malpighi, by the help of exact glasses, observed the first rudiments of it there, both before and after incubation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use magnification ('exact glasses') to detect early rudimentary structures in ova; compare observations before and after incubation; treat repeated independent microscopic observations (e.g., Malpighi, repeated observations de formatione pulli in ovo) as strong evidence for claims about generation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit, testable propositions when proposing a theory of generation
rubrics_metrics.description: Now upon comparing the observations and discoveries which have been made with each other; these three things seem to me very probable. 1. That animals are ex animalculo. 2. That these animalcules are originally in semine marium, et non in foeminis. 3. That they can never come forward, nor be formed into animals of the respective kind, without the ova in foeminis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When advancing a theory, state clear, numbered propositions that are empirically testable and open to corroboration or refutation by observation/experiment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of evidentiary convergence for male-origin hypothesis
rubrics_metrics.description: The 2d thing which later discoveries have made probable is, that these animalcules are originally in semine marium, et non in foeminis. And this I collect from these considerations. 1. That there are innumerable animalcula discovered in semine masculo... 2. The observing the rudiments of the foetus in eggs, which have been fecundated by the male, and the seeing no such thing in those which are not fecundated... 3. The resemblance between the rudiments of the foetus in ovo... and the animalcule...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aggregate multiple independent lines of evidence (presence of animalcules in male semen, differential presence of rudiments in fecundated vs unfecundated eggs, morphological resemblance) to support a causal-origin claim. Emphasize repeated observations and morphological comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessity of a proper nidus (cicatricula/ova) for development
rubrics_metrics.description: That animals cannot be formed of these animalcules without the ova in females, which are necessary for supplying them with proper nutriment... an animalcule cannot come forward, if it do not fall into a proper nidus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require evidence that a specific micro-environment (nidus/cicatricula/ova) is necessary for development: demonstrate that only animalcules located in the proper position (e.g., centre of cicatricula) develop; use analogies with uterus/egg structure and examples (few monsters, eggs cluster fecundated by one coition) to justify the requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimentum crucis (crucial experiment) to test organ necessity
rubrics_metrics.description: To all these I shall subjoin the proposal of an experimentum crucis, which may seem to determine whether the testes foeminei be truly the ovaria, viz. Open the abdomen of the females of some kinds, and cut out these testicles, and this will determine whether they be absolutely necessary for the formation of animals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design and state a decisive experimental manipulation (e.g., surgical removal of putative organs) whose outcome would directly confirm or refute the causal role hypothesized. Provide procedural clarity so others can reproduce the crucial test.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond to objections by anatomical/observational reconciliation
rubrics_metrics.description: There are some difficulties proposed against this conjecture, which I think may be easily resolved. Some object the distance between the tubes or cornua uteri and the testicles ... the great disproportion between the pretended eggs in the ovary, and the aperture of the tubae or cornua uteri ... The difficulty to conceive how these eggs should be impregnated per semen maris ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When objections arise (anatomical distance, size disproportions, mechanistic plausibility), reconcile them with further anatomical observations (glandules, papillae, embracing cornua), comparative examples (hens/frogs), or alternative mechanisms (impregnation in vitellary vs uterus). Use direct dissections and comparative anatomy to answer mechanistic objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use multiple observational types (extra-uterine fetuses, adhesion timing) as inferential support
rubrics_metrics.description: That this cicatricula is not originally in the uterus, seems evident from the frequent conceptions which have been found without the uterus ... that the foetus in the uterus, for some considerable time after conception, has no connection with the womb; that it sits wholly loose from it, and is perfectly a little round egg ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate exceptional clinical/anatomical cases (e.g., extra-uterine fetuses, long gravidations) and developmental timing (delayed adhesion) into inference about origin/location of ova, treating such anomalies as informative evidence rather than mere curiosities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Toxicology experiment protocol and pathological diagnostic signs (mercury injection)
rubrics_metrics.description: I injected into the jugular vein about 14- oz. of crude mercury, and observed the dog soon after to have a dry short cough... The 4th day after the injection of the mercury, he died... I opened him, and found about him a pint of bloody serum extravasated in the thorax... the outside of the lungs in most places blistered ... most of them contained mercurial globules... Opening the right ventricle of the heart, I found some particles of the quicksilver ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document clinical progression after exposure (symptoms, timing), then perform systematic post-mortem examination to locate the substance and lesions (sanies, blisters on lung surface, mercurial globules under bronchia, coagula in heart, extravasated serum). Use distributional findings to infer mechanism (e.g., mercury stopping pulmonary circulation causing blisters). Relate animal-pathology to observed human clinical patterns cautiously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inferential caution when extrapolating from animal experiments to humans
rubrics_metrics.description: From hence may appear the danger of using mercury in human bodies, so as that it may get into the mass of blood, especially into the lungs ... That it has this effect on human lungs, is plain from what we daily see in persons that have been often fluxed, who are after observed to die of consumptions...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare pathological features seen in animal experiments with epidemiological/clinical observations in humans to assess human risk, but ground such extrapolations in mechanistic parallels and observable signs rather than solely in supposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hydrostatics method for authenticating materia medica and solids/fluids
rubrics_metrics.description: By weighing bodies in water, comparing their weight in air, and from thence deducing the proportion of weight to water, the specific gravity of bodies may thence be more exactly determined; counterfeits distinguished from genuine, and the mixture of mineral particles in stone discovered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Archimedean procedure: weigh object in air and in water; difference equals weight of displaced water. Divide weight in air by difference to get proportion relative to water. For bodies lighter than water, add a heavy counterweight (lead) and subtract its contribution. For fluids or dissoluble fragments, place them in a stopped glass phial and account for phial volume when computing weights. To determine fluid density, weigh solids in the fluid and use loss of weight. To estimate bulk, use loss of weight relative to known weight-per-volume of fluid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Astronomical/observational reporting standards (transit of Mercury)
rubrics_metrics.description: The ratio of the diameters of the sun and the nucleus of Mercury, while he continued in the sun's lucid disc, as well as could be judged through the thick air, was as 1000 to 84... After he had adhered near a minute to the undulating limb, and had recovered his genuine roundness... that ratio was as 1000 to 12-i-.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record precise timing of contacts (ingress/egress), note duration of adhesion to limb, record sun altitude and observing conditions (thick air), estimate apparent diameter ratios, and note optical distortions (elliptical appearance due to solar glare) to allow later quantitative inference and correction for atmospheric effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical/chronological reconstruction using primary texts and astronomical data
rubrics_metrics.description: The authors that mention this expedition are Caesar in his Commentaries... From these data, that it was in the year of the Consulate of Pompey and Crassus; that it was Exigua parte aestatis reliqud, and 4 days before a full-moon... the time of this invasion will be determined to a day ... the landing on Britain was August 26, in the afternoon...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use primary textual accounts (Caesar, Dion Cassius), translate/interpret relevant phrases precisely, cross-check with astronomical data (phase of moon, tides), consider seasonal expressions ('exigua parte aestatis reliqud'), and use wind/tide behavior and geographic features to infer date/time/place. Employ Ptolemaic coordinates and modern surveys to corroborate distances and locations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analogical reasoning between plant and animal propagation as supporting inference
rubrics_metrics.description: The analogy between the manner of the propagation of plants and animals likewise makes this probable. Every herb and tree bears its seed after its kind, which seed is nothing else but a little plant of the same kind... we may rationally conjecture some such analogy in the propagation of animals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use well-understood analogies (e.g., seed-to-plant) as heuristic support for biological hypotheses, but treat analogy as supportive rather than conclusive and seek direct observational/experimental corroboration.
